subject: Private pool admission & throughput plan for Nebula Health
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Nebula Health Ops <ops@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-07-11T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Private pool admission & throughput plan kickoff

Team / Tom,

Bringing this thread to start the operational review for Nebula Health's private GPU pool. Goal is to land on an admission policy, baseline throughput guarantees, and a burst strategy we can commit to for the POC (target start: Aug 1). High-level asks below — I've attached the throughput profile CSV and an initial proposal draft.

Summary of customer ask (from Marissa):
- Sustained load: ~700 QPS average over business hours (US-east), typical request size ~600 tokens.
- Peak burst: short 10–15 minute windows up to ~2,000 QPS during batch exports/analytics jobs.
- SLO target: 95th latency < 350ms for interactive calls, best-effort for long-running exports.

Initial constraints we should consider:
- Private pool will be VPC-attached, single-rack to start (12 A100-equivalent GPUs proposed).
- Network egress caps at customer side: they have a 100 Gbps uplink available to the rack.
- Customer requires per-tenant isolation and the ability to carve out reserved QPS for critical services.

Specific asks for this review:
1) Jonas: a short rightsizing calc (baseline GPUs, burst headroom, KV cache sizing) and an admission-policy sketch (per-tenant carveouts, soft quotas, hard limits).
2) Marissa: confirm the commercial carveouts we plan to include in the MAM (reserved QPS / burst credit), and whether that needs changes to the proposal doc.
3) Ops (Tom): confirm expected peak-window characteristics (duration / spike shapes) and any networking constraints on your side we should factor in (eg. cross-rack traffic, egress patterns).

Attachments: nebula-throughput-profiles.csv (profiles by hour), privgpu-proposal-draft.md (draft scope & ops assumptions).

Target follow-up: 48h, with a short call if more than two open questions remain.

Thanks,
Laura

Head of Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Nebula Health Ops <ops@nebulahealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private pool admission & throughput plan kickoff

Laura — quick pass from infra side. High level thoughts and a proposed numeric skeleton.

Key assumptions I used (explicit so we can iterate):
- Average request = 600 tokens in, ~600 tokens out (1.2k tokens total). We’ll size on tokens/sec since tails & batching change CPU/GPU behavior.
- A single A100-equivalent GPU can sustain ~6k tokens/sec for the customer model under our kernel set (quantized), with KV cache warm.

Rightsizing sketch (baseline):
- Sustained target (700 QPS * 1.2k tokens ≈ 840k tokens/sec). That implies ~140 A100-equivalent GPUs if we scaled purely on tokens/sec — this is obviously not the right surface for private pool where we will multiplex. Realistic multiplexing and batching reduces per-token cost by ~6x in our observed traces; use an effective concurrency multiplier of 6.
- Effective GPU count estimate: 140 / 6 ≈ 24 GPUs for sustained profile with ~10% headroom.
- Burst to 2,000 QPS -> transient add of ~2–3x effective load. Plan: baseline 24 GPUs + warm burst capacity to 36 GPUs (autoscale target) with fast warmup via pre-cached KV prefixes.

Admission policy proposal (draft):
1) Per-tenant guaranteed slab: allocate a minimal guaranteed slab (e.g., 20% of baseline tokens/sec) for critical sub-services. This is enforced via soft token buckets plus hard QPS cap.
2) Shared pool: remaining tokens are served from a shared queue with admission control. Use leaky-bucket shaping with a burst credit bucket (credits accumulated during low-util periods).
3) Slow-path handling: requests that exceed available capacity are queued for up to 1s; beyond that return 503 with retry-after header. Exception: scheduled exports (long jobs) should be sent to a batch queue with different SLOs.

Networking / fabric notes:
- Plan for 200 Gbps rack fabric (two 100 G uplinks) to avoid headroom-related queuing; customer 100 G uplink is likely the egress constraint but intra-rack fabric should not be the limiter.
- Per-GPU ephemeral NIC: budget 25–40 Gbps for model-weight fetch and KV sync during cold starts. If we keep KV warm this stays below 10 Gbps steady per GPU.

Operational controls to include in proposal:
- KV prefix warmup ops (automated warm pool prefetch before predicted spikes).
- Autoscale policy: scale-up threshold at 75% sustained tokens/sec for > 2 minutes; scale-down after 10m of <50%. Pre-warm policy to add N GPUs in provisioning state before traffic hits.
- Observability: token-level breakdown per tenant, per-route 95/99 latency, and per-GPU CPU/GPU utilization dashboards.

Open questions for Nebula Ops:
- Do you have any cold-start constraints (no outbound weight downloads, air-gapped steps)?
- Can you support a secondary 100 G uplink or a private peering to help burst egress?

I can drop a short spreadsheet with these numbers (baseline vs burst vs warm-pool) if you'd like.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Platform Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Tom Chen <tom@nebulahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-11T15:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private pool admission & throughput plan kickoff

Laura / Jonas — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side after I ran the profile with ops: 

1) Spike shape: most of our bursts are short, steep (2–12 minutes), caused by periodic analytic jobs kicked off by clinicians. We have a handful of true sustained windows (~1 hour) tied to scheduled reporting.
2) Air-gapped constraints: we are not fully air-gapped, but weight pulls must originate from a pre-approved S3 endpoint (we will whitelist). No outbound peering changes for now.
3) Egress: confirmed single 100 G uplink for this rack. We cannot add a second uplink during the POC window.

Given that:
- We can tolerate a small percentage of 429s during the steepest spikes if they translate to retries. Exports must not be impacted — they can be moved to batch queue.
- We will prepare a short list of critical tenant IDs for the carveouts by EOD Monday.

One ask: can you map the 24->36 GPU plan to a monthly cost delta so procurement has a number to review? If you can attach a staging/prod cost delta that would be ideal.

Tom
Tom Chen
SRE Lead, Nebula Health
ops@nebulahealth.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Chen <tom@nebulahealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-12T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private pool admission & throughput plan kickoff — actions & next steps

Thanks everyone — short summary and action items.

Decisions / agreed plan:
- Rightsize baseline to 24 GPUs (A100-equivalent) as Jonas sketched, with autoscale target up to 36 GPUs for bursts. We will attempt to reduce baseline if early telemetry supports it.
- Admission policy: per-tenant guaranteed slab + shared pool + burst-credit bucket. Exports -> batch queue with different SLOs. 503 after 1s queue limit for interactive requests.
- Networking: proceed with single 100 G uplink constraint; we will design warm-pool prefetching and KV strategies to keep per-GPU steady-state network < 10 Gbps.

Action items (owners):
- Jonas: attach a short spreadsheet mapping baseline vs burst GPU counts to monthly cost estimates and a simple costing for warm-pool pre-warm hours. Deliverable: shared sheet link. (ETA: 48h)
- Marissa: consolidate commercial carveouts and tenant list for reserved slabs; update proposal doc. (ETA: EOD Mon)
- Tom / Nebula: confirm the list of critical tenant IDs and any S3 whitelist details for pre-approved weight downloads. (ETA: EOD Mon)
- Laura: update the privgpu-proposal-draft.md with the admission policy text and proposed SLA language for the POC (ETA: 72h).

Attachments included in this thread: nebula-throughput-profiles.csv, privgpu-proposal-draft.md, qos-carveouts.xlsx. Drive draft: https://drive.redwood.com/nebula/privgpu-proposal-v1. HubSpot deal NEB-4421 is linked for reference.

If no objections, I'll schedule a 30-minute sync with Tom and the three of us on Thursday to finalize the slab numbers.

Best,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
